posts.description: Missouri's Driver Improvement Program keeps the points from a ticket off your license. Who qualifies, the 60-day deadline, Form 4444 and the steps.

posts.content:
## What does the Missouri Driver Improvement Program do?

It stops the points for one ticket from being added to your license. Missouri law calls this a stay of the assessment of points: the Department of Revenue accepts your completed course "in lieu of the assessment of points" (RSMo 302.302.5).

It does not erase the ticket. The Missouri Safety Center, which approves the courses, says the program "will not remove the ticket from the drivers record, only the points." You still pay the fine and court costs.

## Who decides whether you can take it?

The court does. The Safety Center's instruction is that you "must appear in court and request the court's permission," and that the court decides "on a case by case basis." No course provider can approve you, and that includes us.

Ask before you plead guilty or pay. [How to ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) walks through it.

## Which tickets qualify?

The law covers three kinds of points:

- Speeding (3 points under state law, 2 under a city or county ordinance)
- Careless and imprudent driving
- Other ordinary moving violations, which are 2 points each

It also covers the 2 extra points a court can add when a violation caused injury or property damage. Tickets such as driving while intoxicated, leaving the scene, driving while suspended and passing a stopped school bus are outside the program. The full list is in [which tickets qualify](/missouri/blog/which-tickets-qualify-missouri-driver-improvement).

## Who can't use it?

- Anyone who holds a commercial driver license, in Missouri or any other state, or who was driving a commercial vehicle. See [CDL holders](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-cdl).
- Drivers licensed in another state who get a Missouri ticket, and Missouri drivers ticketed in another state. See [out-of-state tickets](/missouri/blog/out-of-state-ticket-missouri-driver-improvement).
- Anyone who used the program in the last 36 months.
- Motorcycle riders ticketed on a motorcycle. They take an approved rider training course instead.

## How long do you have?

Sixty days from the date of your conviction, which is the day you plead guilty or are found guilty. The 60 days are in the statute, so a court usually can't extend them. After you finish, the completion form has to reach the Department of Revenue within 15 days. More in [the 60-day deadline](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-60-day-deadline).

## What are the steps?

1. Get the ticket and respond by the court date on it.
2. Ask the court for the Driver Improvement Program.
3. Plead guilty. The court approves the program and you pay the fine and costs.
4. Take an 8-hour course from the Safety Center's approved list.
5. Get your completion form, MO Form 4444, from the course provider.
6. Take the form to the court clerk for a signature.
7. Mail it to the Department of Revenue, PO Box 200, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200.

Steps 5 to 7 are covered in [Form 4444](/missouri/blog/missouri-form-4444).

## Does the course have to be in a classroom?

No. The statute says you "shall be given the option to complete the driver-improvement program through an online or in-person course." Read your court paperwork anyway, because some orders name the format. See [online or in person](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-online-or-in-person).

## What does it cost?

You pay two things: the court's fine and costs, and the course fee. Our course is $24.99 with the certificate and completion form included. Nothing is added at checkout.

## Is it worth it?

It depends on how many points you already have. Missouri suspends a license at 8 points in 18 months, and one state speeding ticket is 3. If you already have 5, a fourth ticket like that one suspends your license for 30 days. [Check your points](/missouri/blog/check-points-missouri-driving-record) before you decide.

posts.seoTitle: Does Missouri Driver Improvement Remove Points?
posts.description: The Missouri Driver Improvement Program keeps new points off your license. It can't remove points you already have. Here is what clears those.
posts.answer: It keeps the points from one new ticket off your license, if the court approves it and you finish within 60 days. It can't take off points that are already on your record. Those come off with time: a third after one clean year, half of what's left after two, and the rest after three.

faq.a: By one third after one year without a new moving-violation conviction, by half of the remainder after two years, and to zero after three years.

posts.content:
## Does the course take points off your license?

No. It stops points from being added. Missouri law has the Department of Revenue accept a completed course "in lieu of the assessment of points" for the ticket the court approved (RSMo 302.302.5). Points from earlier tickets stay where they are.

## Can I take the course on my own to lower my points?

You can take it, but it won't change your record. The statute only counts a course that was "ordered and verified" by a court for a specific ticket. A course you take without a court's approval isn't reported to the Department of Revenue as a point stay.

We'd rather you know that before you pay us $24.99.

## How do points already on my record come off?

They come off as you drive without a new moving-violation conviction (RSMo 302.306):

| Time without a new conviction | What happens |
|---|---|
| 1 year | Your total drops by one third |
| 2 years | What's left drops by half |
| 3 years | The rest is removed |

Say you have 6 points. After one clean year you have 4. After two you have 2. After three you have none.

## Does the ticket disappear?

No. The Missouri Safety Center says the program "will not remove the ticket from the drivers record, only the points from the license." The Department of Revenue says a ticket conviction may be removed three years after the conviction date. More in [how long points stay on your license](/missouri/blog/how-long-points-stay-on-missouri-license).

## When does keeping the points off matter most?

When you're close to a threshold. The Department of Revenue sends a warning letter at 4 points in 12 months and suspends your license at 8 points in 18 months.

A state speeding ticket is 3 points. If you already have 5, that ticket suspends your license. With the program approved and finished on time, you stay at 5.

## What should I do first?

1. [Check how many points you have](/missouri/blog/check-points-missouri-driving-record). The phone line is free and open all night.
2. If a new ticket is pending, [ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) about the program before you pay.
3. Once the court says yes, [take the course](/missouri) and send in the form inside your 60 days.

posts.content:
## How many points does Missouri give for speeding?

Three points for a conviction under state law and 2 points under a county or municipal ordinance (RSMo 302.302.1(2)). The Department of Revenue's points chart, Form 899, shows the same numbers.

## How do I know which one I was charged with?

Read the citation. It names the law you're charged under. A state charge cites the Missouri statutes, usually RSMo 304.010. A city or county charge cites a local ordinance number and sends you to a municipal court.

## Does going faster mean more points?

No. Ten over and twenty-four over are the same number of points. What changes is the fine, and at 20 mph or more over the limit the charge rises from a class C misdemeanor to a class B misdemeanor (RSMo 304.010.11). Fines are in [what a Missouri speeding ticket costs](/missouri/blog/missouri-speeding-ticket-cost).

## Is there a speed that carries no points?

Yes. Missouri law says "no points shall be assessed" for speeding that is over the posted limit by five miles per hour or less (RSMo 304.009). That ticket is an infraction. You still owe the fine and court costs.

## Can a speeding ticket carry more than 3 points?

Yes, if someone was hurt or property was damaged. The court can certify that, and the Department of Revenue adds 2 points (RSMo 302.302.3).

## How do I keep speeding points off my license?

Ask the court for the Driver Improvement Program before you plead guilty or pay. Speeding is one of the violations the program covers. If the court approves it and you finish an 8-hour course within 60 days of your conviction, the points are not added.

Three things rule it out: a commercial driver license, an out-of-state license, or having used the program in the last 36 months.

## How close is one speeding ticket to a suspension?

Missouri suspends at 8 points in 18 months. Three state speeding tickets in a year and a half is 9 points. The Department of Revenue sends a warning letter at 4 points in 12 months, which is two tickets for most drivers. [What 4, 8 and 12 points do](/missouri/blog/missouri-points-what-4-8-12-points-do) has the full table.

posts.content:
## What is the fine for speeding in Missouri?

For a state charge that can be paid without a court appearance, the fine comes from the State Traffic Fine Schedule published by the Missouri courts:

| Speed over the posted limit | Fine |
|---|---|
| 1 to 5 mph | $50.50 |
| 6 to 10 mph | $60.50 |
| 11 to 15 mph | $80.50 |
| 16 to 19 mph | $120.50 |
| 20 to 25 mph | $200.50 |

These are the fines only. Court costs are added on top. The schedule we read is the one posted on the courts' Statewide Fine Schedule page on September 29, 2026.

## How do I find my exact total?

Look up your case on Case.net with your citation number and click Plead and Pay. It shows the fine plus court costs. The courts say looking does not plead you guilty. You're only pleading guilty when you finish the payment and get a confirmation.

## What if I was more than 25 over?

The schedule stops at 25 mph over. Above that, expect to deal with the court directly. Your citation lists the court and the date.

## Is a city speeding ticket the same price?

Not always. Municipal tickets use a separate Municipal Fine Schedule, and the court named on your citation sets the total. Call the clerk or look the case up on Case.net.

## What does the ticket cost besides the fine?

Points. A state speeding conviction is 3 points and a local one is 2. Eight points in 18 months suspends your license, and getting it back costs a $20 reinstatement fee plus two years of SR-22 insurance filings.

Your insurer can also see the conviction. The Missouri Department of Commerce and Insurance lists your driving record among the things companies usually base rates on.

## Can I lower what the ticket costs me?

You can't lower the fine with a course. You can keep the points off. If the court approves the Driver Improvement Program, you pay the fine and costs, take an 8-hour course within 60 days, and the points are not added. Our course is $24.99.

Ask the court before you pay. [Should I just pay my ticket online?](/missouri/blog/should-i-pay-my-missouri-ticket-online) explains why the order matters.

posts.content:
## How many points is each violation in Missouri?

These come from the Department of Revenue's Form 899, revised in August 2026, and RSMo 302.302.

| Violation | State law | County or city ordinance | Driver Improvement Program? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speeding, more than 5 mph over | 3 | 2 | Yes |
| Speeding, 5 mph over or less | 0 | 0 | No points to stay |
| Stop sign | 2 | 2 county, 1 city | Yes |
| Following too close | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| Failure to yield | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| Improper lane, turn or passing | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| Careless and imprudent driving | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| Careless and imprudent under RSMo 304.016 | 4 | 2 | Yes |
| Any moving violation not listed | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| No proof of insurance | 4 | 4 | No |
| Letting an unlicensed driver drive | 4 | 4 | No |
| Endangering a highway worker or emergency responder | 4 | | No |
| Passing a stopped school bus | 5 | | No |
| Driving without a license, first conviction | 2 | 2 | No |
| Driving while intoxicated, first conviction | 8 | 8 | No |
| Driving while intoxicated, later convictions | 12 | 12 | No |
| Leaving the scene of an accident | 12 | 6 | No |
| Driving while suspended or revoked | 12 | 12 | No |
| Felony involving a motor vehicle | 12 | | No |

A court can add 2 points when a violation caused injury or property damage.

## Which violations carry no points?

- Speeding by 5 mph or less over the limit (RSMo 304.009).
- Texting while driving and handheld phone use. Form 899 marks both as no longer point-assessable after August 28, 2023.
- Equipment violations. The points law applies to moving violations "other than a violation of vehicle equipment provisions."

You still pay the fine on all of them.

## Which points can the Driver Improvement Program keep off?

Three groups, named in RSMo 302.302.5: ordinary moving violations, speeding, and careless and imprudent driving. It also covers the 2 extra points for injury or property damage. Nothing else in the table qualifies. [Which tickets qualify](/missouri/blog/which-tickets-qualify-missouri-driver-improvement) goes through the exclusions.

## What changed in 2026?

Passing a school bus that is stopped to load or unload students now carries 5 points. It was added to RSMo 302.302 effective August 28, 2026, and it appears on the August 2026 revision of Form 899. Older charts don't show it.

## When are points added?

Only after a conviction or a forfeiture of collateral. Paying a ticket counts as a conviction. If you want the Driver Improvement Program, [ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) before you pay.

posts.content:
## How long do points stay on a Missouri license?

Up to three years, and they shrink along the way. Under RSMo 302.306:

- After the first full year without a moving-violation conviction, your total is reduced by one third.
- After the second year in a row, what remains is reduced by one half.
- After the third year in a row, the rest is withdrawn.

Start with 6 points and you have 4 after a year, 2 after two years and none after three.

Some websites say the second-year cut is another one third. The statute says one half.

## What resets the clock?

A new conviction for a moving violation. The reduction is for years driven "without conviction for a moving violation," so a new ticket that ends in a conviction starts the count again.

After a point suspension or revocation ends, the Department of Revenue sets your total to 4 points, and the yearly reduction runs from there.

## How long does the ticket stay on my record?

Longer than the points. The Department of Revenue says ticket convictions may be removed three years after the conviction. If the ticket led to a point suspension or revocation, it can be purged five years from the reinstatement date.

The Department also says some convictions "must remain listed permanently," and that the timelines vary by class of license.

## Do I have to ask for an old ticket to be removed?

You can. The Department of Revenue takes purge requests by email at dlbmail@dor.mo.gov, by phone at 573-526-2407, or by mail to PO Box 200, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200. Include your full name and your driver license number.

## Do points matter after they drop?

The suspension rules look at short windows: 8 points in 18 months, or 12 in 12 months for a revocation. Old points that have been reduced count for less, but a new ticket adds its full value on the day you're convicted.

## How do I keep a new ticket from adding points?

Ask the court for the Driver Improvement Program. If it's approved and you finish within 60 days, the points for that ticket are never added, so there's nothing to wait out. You can use it once in any 36 months. [How the program works](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-program).

posts.content:
## How do I find out how many points I have in Missouri?

The quickest way is the phone. The Department of Revenue's interactive voice line at 573-526-2407 gives ticket, suspension and revocation information from your record, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. You can also email dlbmail@dor.mo.gov or log in to your MyDMV profile.

## How do I get a copy of my Missouri driving record?

There are three ways, all from the Department of Revenue:

1. **In person.** Take your photo ID to any Missouri license office and pay the fee.
2. **By mail, email or fax.** Fill out Form 4681, Request from Driver License Record Holder. Every field has to be completed, including your signature and a notary's signature. Send it with the fee to the Driver License Record Center.
3. **Online.** MyDMV sells records that leave out personal information and show only the driving history, such as tickets. The record is emailed to you.

## How much does a Missouri driving record cost?

$2.82 per record. License offices add a $2 processing fee. A faxed record costs $0.50 a page on top.

## What should I look for on the record?

- **Each conviction and its date.** The point thresholds count from conviction dates.
- **Points in the last 12 and 18 months.** Four points in 12 months brings a warning letter. Eight in 18 months brings a suspension.
- **Department actions.** Any suspension or revocation is listed here with its reason.
- **A past Driver Improvement Program.** You can use it once in any 36 months, so an earlier one may rule out another.

## I have a new ticket. When should I check?

Before your court date. If the new ticket would put you at or near 8 points, that's the time to [ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) for the Driver Improvement Program. It keeps the new points from being added, but only if you ask before you plead guilty or pay.

## Will my points be lower than I expect?

They might. Points drop by a third after a year without a new conviction, and by half of what's left after two. [How long points stay on your license](/missouri/blog/how-long-points-stay-on-missouri-license) has the math.

posts.content:
## What is MO Form 4444?

It's the form that tells the Department of Revenue you finished an approved Driver Improvement Program for a specific ticket. Without it, the Department has no record of the course and the points are added.

## Where do I get Form 4444?

From the provider of your course. The Missouri Safety Center's process chart shows the driver receiving "MO Form 4444 from course provider" after the course. Ours is ready to download, along with your certificate, the moment you pass the final quiz.

## Who has to sign it?

The court. The Safety Center's chart has the driver take the form "back to court clerk for signature" before it goes to the state. That matches the law, which only counts a course "ordered and verified" by the court.

Courts handle this differently. Some sign it at the window, some take it by email, and some send it to the state themselves. Call the clerk and ask which one your court does.

## Where do I send it?

Missouri Department of Revenue, Driver License Bureau
PO Box 200
Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200

The Department of Revenue says "you or the program may mail the completion form" to that address. Give the court a copy too if it asked for proof. The Creve Coeur Municipal Court, for example, tells drivers to submit the completion to the court and to the Department of Revenue.

## What is the deadline?

There are two.

- **The course:** finished within 60 days of your conviction date.
- **The form:** at the Department of Revenue within 15 days of finishing the course.

Do both inside the 60 days if you can. If you finish on day 20, you don't need to think about either one again.

## What should I keep?

- A copy of the signed form
- Your certificate of completion
- Proof of mailing, such as a certified mail receipt

Then check your record a few weeks later. [The phone line](/missouri/blog/check-points-missouri-driving-record) is free.

## What if points show up anyway?

Call the Department of Revenue at 573-526-2407 or email dlbmail@dor.mo.gov with your copy of the form and the mailing receipt. Then call the court clerk. This is why you keep copies.

posts.content:
## When does the 60 days start?

On your conviction date. RSMo 302.302 says the program must "be completed within sixty days of the date of conviction." You're convicted the day you plead guilty or are found guilty. Paying a ticket counts: the law treats payment as a guilty plea and a conviction.

The clock does not start when you enroll in a course.

## Can the court give me more time?

Usually not. The 60 days come from state law, not from the court. The Creve Coeur Municipal Court tells drivers that in many instances these deadlines "may NOT be extended by this court as they are state statute regulated."

If something serious gets in the way, call the clerk before day 60. Don't assume.

## What happens if I miss it?

The course isn't accepted in place of the points, and the Department of Revenue adds them. A state speeding ticket is 3 points. You've also paid for a course that didn't do what you bought it for.

## How long does the course take?

Eight hours. Ours is self-paced, saves your place, and ends with a 25-question final. Most people finish across three or four sittings.

## What is a safe schedule?

| When | What to do |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Court approves the program. Write down the conviction date. Enroll. |
| Days 2 to 14 | Finish the 8 hours and pass the final. |
| Days 15 to 21 | Take Form 4444 to the court clerk to sign and get it to the Department of Revenue. Count 15 days from the day you finished the course, not from day 1. Keep proof. |

That leaves a month for anything that goes wrong: a closed clerk's office, a lost envelope, a failed quiz attempt.

## Is there a second deadline?

Yes. The Missouri Safety Center says Form 4444 must get to the Department of Revenue within 15 days of finishing the course. [Form 4444](/missouri/blog/missouri-form-4444) covers who signs it and where it goes.

## I'm on day 50. Is it too late?

Not yet. Eight hours fits in two days. Enroll today, finish tomorrow, and take the form to the clerk in person the day after. Then mail it with tracking.

posts.content:
## Which violations does the program cover?

RSMo 302.302.5 lists them by reference to the points table. The program is accepted in place of points for:

- **Subdivision (1):** any moving violation not listed elsewhere in the table. These are 2 points. Stop signs, red lights, failure to yield, following too close, improper lane use, improper turns and improper passing are all here.
- **Subdivision (2):** speeding. 3 points under state law, 2 under a local ordinance.
- **Subdivision (4):** careless and imprudent driving. 4 points under state law, 2 under a local ordinance.
- **Subsection 3:** the 2 extra points added when a violation caused injury or property damage.

## Which violations are left out?

Everything else in the points table:

| Violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Leaving the scene of an accident | 12 state, 6 local |
| Driving without a valid license | 2, 4 or 6 |
| Driving while suspended or revoked | 12 |
| Getting a license by misrepresentation | 12 |
| Driving while intoxicated or with excess blood alcohol | 8 or 12 |
| Felony involving a motor vehicle | 12 |
| Letting an unlicensed person drive | 4 |
| No insurance | 4 |
| Endangering a highway worker or emergency responder | 4 or 12 |
| Passing a stopped school bus | 5 |

## Does a qualifying ticket mean I'm approved?

No. The Missouri Safety Center says the court decides "on a case by case basis and there is no guarantee that the court will allow you to attend." A qualifying ticket means the court is allowed to say yes.

## Who is ruled out even with a qualifying ticket?

- [CDL holders](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-cdl), and anyone ticketed in a commercial vehicle
- [Drivers licensed in another state](/missouri/blog/out-of-state-ticket-missouri-driver-improvement)
- Anyone who used the program [in the last 36 months](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-once-every-36-months)

## What about a ticket on a motorcycle?

The course is different. For a violation committed on a motorcycle, the law calls for an approved motorcycle-rider training course in place of the Driver Improvement Program. Our course doesn't satisfy that.

## Do I need the program for a ticket with no points?

No. Speeding by 5 mph or less, texting and equipment violations carry no points in Missouri, so there is nothing for the program to keep off.

## What should I do with a qualifying ticket?

[Ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) before you plead guilty or pay. Once it's approved, [take the course](/missouri) within 60 days.

posts.content:
## Can a CDL holder take the Driver Improvement Program in Missouri?

Not to keep points off. RSMo 302.302.5 accepts the program for violations "other than a violation committed in a commercial motor vehicle" or "a violation committed by an individual who has been issued a commercial driver's license or is required to obtain a commercial driver's license in this state or any other state."

The Missouri Safety Center puts it in one line: you cannot participate "if you possess a Commercial Driver License (CDL)."

## Does it matter that I was in my personal car?

No. The second half of the exclusion is about the driver, not the vehicle. If you hold a CDL, a speeding ticket in your pickup on a Sunday is excluded the same as one in the truck.

## Does it matter that my CDL is from another state?

No. The statute says "this state or any other state."

## I drive a commercial vehicle but don't have a CDL. Am I excluded?

If the ticket was written while you were driving a commercial motor vehicle, yes. The law also excludes a driver who "is required to obtain" a CDL.

## Should a CDL holder buy the course anyway?

Not for this. We'd be taking $24.99 for a course that can't do what you need. If a court orders you to take a driving course as part of a sentence or probation, that's a different purpose, and the court's paperwork will say so.

## What can a CDL holder do about a ticket?

Talk to the court or the prosecutor before you plead, and think about talking to an attorney. A moving violation can count toward CDL disqualification as well as points. The Department of Revenue's points chart marks the violations that are used toward disqualification under RSMo 302.700 to 302.780.

We don't give legal advice, and the right step depends on the charge and your record.

## Do points still come off a CDL holder's record over time?

Yes. Points on your base driving privilege are reduced the same way as anyone's: by a third after one year without a new conviction, by half of the remainder after two, and to zero after three. See [how long points stay](/missouri/blog/how-long-points-stay-on-missouri-license).

posts.content:
## I'm from another state and got a ticket in Missouri. Can I take the course?

Not to keep points off. The Missouri Safety Center's process sheet says the program "does not apply to out-of-state licensed drivers receiving a Missouri ticket."

## What happens to my Missouri ticket, then?

Missouri reports it to your home state. The Department of Revenue says that when a driver from another state is convicted of a point-assessable violation in Missouri, the conviction "will then be forwarded to the driver licensing agency in that person's home state for any necessary processing."

What your home state does with it depends on that state's rules. Call your own licensing agency and ask.

## I have a Missouri license and got a ticket in another state. Can I take the course?

No. The Safety Center's sheet also rules out "Missouri licensed drivers receiving a ticket in another state." A Missouri court has to order and verify the course, and there's no Missouri court in an out-of-state case.

## Will an out-of-state ticket put points on my Missouri license?

It can. The Department of Revenue says that when it's notified of a Missouri driver's conviction in another state or on federal property, "our staff will post the ticket to that person's Missouri driver record. The point value is determined by the violation conviction code."

## Should I buy the Missouri course in either case?

No. It won't change your record, and we'd rather not sell it to you.

Ask the court in the state where you got the ticket what it offers. Some states run their own programs for drivers ticketed there.

## I still have to respond to the Missouri ticket, right?

Yes. The Missouri courts say you must respond by the court date on the citation, either by pleading guilty and paying or by appearing and pleading not guilty. Not responding can lead to a suspension and a warrant.

## I just moved to Missouri. Which license counts?

The one you held when you were ticketed decides how the ticket is handled. If you've since switched to a Missouri license and the ticket is in a Missouri court, ask the clerk whether the court will approve the program. The court decides each case.

posts.content:
## What happens when I pay a Missouri ticket online?

You plead guilty. The Missouri courts say that by using Plead and Pay on Case.net, you acknowledge "the payment in full is considered a guilty plea and waiver of a court hearing." State law says the same about paying through the central violations bureau: payment is "a plea of guilty, waiver of trial and a conviction" for the points law (RSMo 476.385).

Points are assessed after a conviction. So the payment is the step that puts them on your license.

## What are my options when I get a ticket?

The courts list them:

1. Plead guilty and pay through Plead and Pay on Case.net, if your case shows the Plead and Pay icon.
2. Mail the signed plea of guilty and waiver that came with the citation, with a check or money order.
3. Pay at the court listed on the citation.
4. Plead not guilty by appearing on the court date on the citation.

You have to do one of them by the court date.

## Where does the Driver Improvement Program fit?

Between deciding to plead guilty and paying. The Missouri Safety Center says a driver "must appear in court and request the court's permission" to take the program. If you pay online first, you've pleaded guilty without asking.

Call the clerk of the court on your citation and ask two questions:

- Will the court let me complete the Driver Improvement Program for this ticket?
- How do I request it: at an appearance, in writing, or when I pay?

## Can I get the program if I've already paid?

Call the clerk right away and ask. Missouri law says a person who pays through the central bureau "consents to attendance either online or in person at any driver-improvement program" the court orders, so some courts can still order it. Whether yours will is up to the court. Your 60 days started on the day you paid.

## Is it ever fine to just pay?

Yes, in a few cases:

- The ticket carries no points, such as speeding by 5 mph or less.
- You can't use the program anyway, because you hold a CDL, have an out-of-state license, or used it in the last 36 months.
- You have no points, and you'd rather save the program for later. You only get it once every 36 months.

## What if I do nothing?

The courts say failure to respond may result in suspension of your driver's license, and a warrant may be issued for your arrest. Under RSMo 302.341 the court notifies the Department of Revenue, and the suspension stays until the ticket is resolved and paid.

## How much will I owe?

Look up the case on Case.net and click Plead and Pay to see the fine and court costs. Looking doesn't plead you guilty. The fines for state speeding tickets are in [what a Missouri speeding ticket costs](/missouri/blog/missouri-speeding-ticket-cost).

posts.content:
## Can I take the Missouri Driver Improvement Program online?

Yes. The option is written into RSMo 302.302.5, and it has been since March 3, 2014. The Missouri Safety Center lists approved online programs and approved classroom locations on the same page.

## Can a court require a classroom?

Read your paperwork. A court can order a driving course for reasons other than points, such as a condition of probation, and those orders can name a format. The Creve Coeur Municipal Court tells drivers to "review your court ordered information to determine what type of program is required (in-person vs virtual)."

If your order is for the Driver Improvement Program in place of points and it says nothing about format, the statute gives you the choice. If you're not sure which kind of order you have, ask the clerk.

## What is the same either way?

- **Eight hours.** The law requires the program to meet or exceed the National Safety Council's 8-hour Defensive Driving Course.
- **The approved list.** The Safety Center says the course "must be on the approved list."
- **The deadline.** Sixty days from your conviction.
- **The form.** MO Form 4444, signed by the court and sent to the Department of Revenue.

## What is different?

| | Online | In person |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule | Any time, in as many sittings as you like | A set class date |
| Where | Phone, tablet or computer | A classroom in one of nine regions of the state |
| Pace | Your own, with your place saved | The instructor's |
| Completion form | From the provider when you pass | From the provider at the end of class |

## Which is faster?

Online is usually sooner to start, because there's no class date to wait for. The 8 hours are the same. With a 60-day deadline, starting this week matters more than the format.

## How do I know a course is approved?

Look it up on the Missouri Safety Center's Driver Improvement Program page. Each approved online program is listed with a program number. If a course isn't on that page, the state won't accept it.

## What is our course like?

Eight hours online, 12 modules, and just one 25-question quiz at the end, with unlimited retakes. It's $24.99 with the certificate and completion form included. [What to expect](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-course-what-to-expect) has the details.

faq.q: How often can you take the Driver Improvement Program in Missouri?

faq.q: Can I take the Missouri Driver Improvement Program twice?

faq.q: What happens if I get a second ticket within 36 months in Missouri?

posts.content:
## How often can I use the program to keep points off?

Once every 36 months. The limit is in RSMo 302.302.5, and the Missouri Safety Center repeats it: "You cannot participate in D.I.P. more than once in a 36 month period of time."

## I used it two years ago and got another ticket. What now?

The court can't approve it for points on this ticket. If you're convicted, the points are added.

How much that matters depends on your total. One 2-point or 3-point ticket on a clean record is below every threshold. The Department of Revenue sends a warning letter at 4 points in 12 months and suspends at 8 in 18 months. [Check your points](/missouri/blog/check-points-missouri-driving-record) before your court date.

## How do I know exactly when my 36 months end?

Ask the Department of Revenue, which keeps the record. The statute doesn't spell out which dates start and end the period. If your last course was about three years ago, call 573-526-2407 or email dlbmail@dor.mo.gov before you plead, and tell the court what you find.

## Should I save the program for a worse ticket?

It's a fair question if your record is clean. Consider:

- A 3-point ticket on a clean record puts you at 3. Nothing happens at 3.
- Points shrink with time. Three points become 2 after a clean year.
- A second ticket within 18 months is when the numbers start to matter.

If you drive a lot, or you already have points, use it now. If your record is clean and this is a 2-point city ticket, keeping it in reserve can make sense. It's your call, and either choice is reasonable.

## Does the limit apply to courses I take for other reasons?

The limit is on courses accepted in place of points. A course a court orders as part of probation isn't a point stay. Ask the clerk which kind of order you have.

## Can I use it for two tickets from the same stop?

The statute is written around completing the program for "a violation," and it limits acceptance to one time in 36 months. If you were cited for two violations at once, ask the court how it will handle them before you plead to either.

## What else keeps my points down?

Time. Points drop by a third after a year without a new conviction, by half of the rest after two, and to zero after three. See [how long points stay on your license](/missouri/blog/how-long-points-stay-on-missouri-license).

posts.content:
## How many points suspend a license in Missouri?

Eight points in 18 months (RSMo 302.304). The Department of Revenue also sends a warning letter when you reach 4 points in 12 months.

## How long is a points suspension?

- First suspension: 30 days
- Second suspension: 60 days
- Third and later suspensions: 90 days

Those lengths apply if you file proof of insurance. The statute says that unless proof of financial responsibility is filed, "a suspension shall continue in effect for two years from its effective date."

## What is the difference between a suspension and a revocation?

A revocation is longer, and you have to test again. Missouri revokes for one year at 12 points in 12 months, 18 points in 24 months, or 24 points in 36 months. After a revocation you retake the complete driver exam.

## How do I get my license back after a points suspension?

For points from non-alcohol violations such as speeding, the Department of Revenue requires two things:

1. Pay the $20 reinstatement fee.
2. File proof of liability insurance on an SR-22 form, and keep it on file for two years from the start date of the suspension.

You can pay online at mydmv.mo.gov, by mail, or in person at the Jefferson City central office. You can't pay at a local license office. Card payments carry a convenience fee of 2.0% plus $0.25.

## What happens to my points afterward?

They're reduced to 4 when you're reinstated. From there they drop each year you go without a new conviction.

## Can I drive to work during the suspension?

Only with a Limited Driving Privilege. The Department of Revenue says you cannot drive while suspended "unless you apply for and receive a Limited Driving Privilege (LDP)." Driving while suspended is a 12-point conviction, which is a revocation.

## Can I appeal?

Yes. You can appeal in the circuit court of the county where you live within 30 days after the notice is issued.

## Can the Driver Improvement Program undo a suspension?

No. It keeps the points from a new ticket from being added. It can't remove points already counted, and it isn't a reinstatement requirement.

It helps before the suspension. If you have 5 or 6 points and a new ticket, [ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) for the program before you plead. With the points kept off, you stay under 8.

Missouri doesn't set insurance rates or require a lower rate for taking the course. It does help you avoid a suspension, which would mean two years of SR-22 filings.

posts.content:
## Will my insurance company see the ticket if I take the course?

Yes. The Missouri Safety Center says the program "will not remove the ticket from the drivers record, only the points from the license." Your record still shows the conviction. The Department of Revenue says a ticket conviction may be removed three years after the conviction date.

Some course websites say insurers won't see the ticket. The state's own documents say the conviction stays.

## Does Missouri make insurers lower rates for taking the course?

No. The Missouri Department of Commerce and Insurance says it "does not set insurance rates." Nothing in the Driver Improvement Program law mentions insurance.

## What do insurers base rates on?

The Department of Commerce and Insurance lists what companies usually use: the coverage and deductible you choose, where the car is kept, how it's used, the car itself, the driver's age and sex, credit history, and "driving and claims record."

Each company decides how much a ticket counts. Some look at convictions. Some look at points. The only way to know is to ask yours.

## What should I ask my insurance company?

- Do you raise rates for a conviction that has no points assessed?
- How many years back do you look at my driving record?
- Do you lower my rate if I finish a defensive driving course on my own?

Get the answers before your court date. They're part of deciding whether to use the program now or save it.

## How does the course help with insurance at all?

It helps you stay below a suspension. Eight points in 18 months suspends your license, and to get it back you file an SR-22 form and keep it on file for two years. An SR-22 is a filing your insurer makes to prove you carry liability coverage.

If you have 5 points and a 3-point ticket, the program is what keeps you at 5.

## So is the course worth $24.99?

For your license, yes, if the court approves it and you have points or drive enough to pick up more. For your insurance bill, we can't promise anything, and neither can anyone else selling a course.

[How the program works](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-program) covers who qualifies.

posts.content:
## How long is the Missouri Driver Improvement Program?

Eight hours. That comes from state law, which requires the program to "meet or exceed the standards of the National Safety Council's eight-hour Defensive Driving Course." Every approved course is 8 hours, whoever sells it.

Each of our modules has a minimum time, and together they add up to the 8 hours. You can't finish faster than that. You can stop and come back as often as you like.

## What does the course cover?

Twelve modules:

1. Introduction and orientation
2. Traffic laws and why they matter
3. Defensive driving techniques
4. The psychology of driving
5. Impaired driving
6. Sharing the road
7. Crash dynamics and avoidance
8. The vehicle and driving environment
9. Risk and how to manage it
10. Preparing to drive
11. The six unsafe behaviors
12. Driving for life

Then the final quiz.

## Is there a test?

One. The final quiz is 25 questions, and 20 correct passes. There are no other quizzes.

## What if I fail the final?

Take it again. Retakes are unlimited, there's no waiting period, and the questions are different each time. We don't charge for them.

## Can I do it on my phone?

Yes. The course and the quiz work in a phone's browser. Your progress saves when you leave, so you can switch between your phone and a computer.

## What do I need to enroll?

- Your name, date of birth and Missouri driver license number, as they appear on your license
- Your court and citation details, so they appear on your completion form
- A card for the $24.99

Have the court's approval before you enroll. The Missouri Safety Center says you need a conviction date before you take the course, and the court is the one that decides whether you can use the program.

## What do I get when I pass?

Your certificate of completion and the completion form, MO Form 4444, ready to download the moment you pass. [Form 4444](/missouri/blog/missouri-form-4444) explains who signs it and where to mail it.

## How should I plan the 8 hours?

Most people finish across three or four sittings. Two hours on four evenings does it. You have [60 days from your conviction](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-60-day-deadline), and we'd finish in the first two weeks.

## What if I change my mind?

You get a full refund any time before you complete the course. After you pass and the certificate is issued, there's no refund.

## Who do I call with a problem?

Us. Support is by phone at (888) 885-5707 and by email at info@roadreadysafety.com.

posts.content:
## Who approves the Driver Improvement Program?

The court handling your ticket. The Missouri Safety Center says the court "has the authority to allow you to attend DIP to avoid point assessment," and that the decision "is made by the court on a case by case basis." The Department of Revenue records the result. It doesn't approve anyone.

## How do I ask?

1. **Find your court.** It's printed on the citation, with a court date.
2. **Call or email the clerk before that date.** Say you'd like to complete the Driver Improvement Program so the points for this ticket aren't assessed, and ask how the court handles the request.
3. **Do what the clerk tells you.** Some courts want you to appear. Some have a form. Some prosecutors offer it as part of a plea.
4. **Get the approval in writing** if you can, with the date of your plea.

## What should I say?

Keep it short:

> I have a citation for [violation], number [citation number], with a court date of [date]. I have a Missouri license and I don't hold a CDL. I'd like to ask the court to let me complete the Driver Improvement Program under RSMo 302.302 so the points aren't assessed. How do I request that?

## What will the court want to know?

- Whether you hold a commercial driver license. If you do, you can't use the program.
- Whether you've used the program in the last 36 months.
- What the ticket is for. Only [certain violations qualify](/missouri/blog/which-tickets-qualify-missouri-driver-improvement).

## Can the court say no?

Yes. The Safety Center says "there is no guarantee that the court will allow you to attend DIP." If the answer is no, ask the clerk or the prosecutor what other options the court offers, or talk to an attorney.

## What about the Fine Collection Center?

The Department of Revenue's FAQ still says "the court or the Fine Collections Center may authorize" the program. The Missouri courts now handle pay-without-appearing tickets through Plead and Pay on Case.net, which launched in 2019. Either way, the court on your citation is the one to ask.

## What happens after the court says yes?

1. Pay the fine and court costs. The program doesn't replace them.
2. [Take an approved 8-hour course](/missouri) within 60 days of your conviction.
3. Get MO Form 4444 from the course provider and take it to the court clerk for a signature.
4. Mail it to the Department of Revenue within 15 days of finishing.

[Form 4444](/missouri/blog/missouri-form-4444) and [the 60-day deadline](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-60-day-deadline) cover those steps.

## Should I enroll before the court answers?

No. The Safety Center says you "must have a conviction date before you can enroll and take an approved D.I.P. class." If you enroll with us and the court then says no, we refund you in full, as long as you haven't finished the course.

posts.title: Missouri points: what 4, 8 and 12 points do to your license
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Points: What 4, 8 and 12 Points Do
posts.description: Four points in 12 months brings a warning letter. Eight in 18 months suspends a Missouri license. Twelve in 12 months revokes it for a year.
posts.answer: Four points in 12 months gets you a warning letter from the Department of Revenue. Eight points in 18 months suspends your license for 30, 60 or 90 days. Twelve points in 12 months, 18 in 24, or 24 in 36 revokes it for one year.

faq.q: How many points suspends a Missouri license?
faq.a: Eight points in 18 months. The suspension is 30 days for a first suspension, 60 days for a second and 90 days for a third or later one.

faq.q: How many points revokes a Missouri license?
faq.a: Twelve points in 12 months, 18 points in 24 months, or 24 points in 36 months. The revocation lasts one year.

faq.q: What happens at 4 points in Missouri?
faq.a: The Department of Revenue mails you a point accumulation advisory letter when you reach 4 points in 12 months. Your license is not suspended.

faq.q: How do Missouri points come off?
faq.a: By one third after one year without a new moving-violation conviction, by half of the remainder after two years, and entirely after three years.

posts.content:
## What are Missouri's point thresholds?

| Points | Within | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 12 months | The Department of Revenue mails you a point accumulation advisory letter |
| 8 | 18 months | Suspension: 30 days the first time, 60 the second, 90 the third and after |
| 12 | 12 months | Revocation for one year |
| 18 | 24 months | Revocation for one year |
| 24 | 36 months | Revocation for one year |

These are in RSMo 302.304. Points count from the date of conviction.

## How fast do points add up?

Most moving violations are 2 points. Speeding is 3 points under state law and 2 under a city or county ordinance. So:

- Two tickets in a year can reach 4 and bring the warning letter.
- Three state speeding tickets in 18 months is 9, which is a suspension.

The serious offenses reach a threshold in one conviction. A first DWI is 8 points. Driving while suspended and leaving the scene under state law are 12. [Points by violation](/missouri/blog/missouri-points-by-violation) has the chart.

## What does a suspension cost me?

Thirty days without driving the first time, a $20 reinstatement fee, and an SR-22 insurance filing that you keep for two years. If you don't file the SR-22, the suspension runs two years. See [suspended for points](/missouri/blog/missouri-license-suspended-for-points).

## What does a revocation cost me?

A year without a license, the same fee and SR-22, and then the complete driver exam again.

## How do points come off?

Each year you drive without a new moving-violation conviction:

- After one year, your total drops by a third.
- After two years, what's left drops by half.
- After three years, the rest is removed.

After a suspension or revocation ends, your total is set to 4.

## Where does the Driver Improvement Program fit?

It keeps the points from a new ticket from being added, if the court approves it and you finish an 8-hour course within 60 days of your conviction. It doesn't remove points you already have. You can use it once in any 36 months.

If you have 6 points and a new 2-point ticket, that ticket is the one that suspends you. With the program, you stay at 6.

## What should I do today?

1. [Check your points](/missouri/blog/check-points-missouri-driving-record). Call 573-526-2407 any time.
2. If a ticket is pending, [ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program) about the program before you plead or pay.
3. If you're already suspended, read your notice. The program isn't part of reinstatement.

posts.title: Careless and imprudent driving in Missouri: points and penalties
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Careless and Imprudent Driving Ticket
posts.description: Careless and imprudent driving is a class B misdemeanor in Missouri, or class A with an accident. The points, and whether a course can keep them off.
posts.answer: Careless and imprudent driving is a class B misdemeanor in Missouri, and a class A misdemeanor if an accident is involved. It carries 2 to 4 points depending on the charge. It's one of the three kinds of violation the Driver Improvement Program covers, so a court can let you take the course to keep the points off.

faq.a: Yes. It is a class B misdemeanor under RSMo 304.012, or a class A misdemeanor if an accident is involved.

faq.a: Two points, or 4 points for a state conviction under RSMo 304.016, according to Department of Revenue Form 899.

faq.a: Yes, if the court approves it. RSMo 302.302 lists careless and imprudent driving among the violations the program covers.

posts.content:
## What is careless and imprudent driving?

RSMo 304.012 requires every driver to drive "in a careful and prudent manner and at a rate of speed so as not to endanger the property of another or the life or limb of any person" and to "exercise the highest degree of care."

Since August 28, 2025, the same section also bans stunt driving.

## What is the penalty?

A class B misdemeanor, "unless an accident is involved then it shall be a class A misdemeanor." The court sets the fine and any other sentence.

## How many points is it?

The Department of Revenue's points chart, Form 899, has two lines:

| Charge | State law | County or city ordinance |
|---|---|---|
| Careless and imprudent | 2 | 2 |
| Careless and imprudent under RSMo 304.016 | 4 | 2 |

A court can add 2 more points if the violation caused injury or property damage.

## Can I pay it online?

Probably not. Careless and imprudent driving isn't on the statewide fine schedule for tickets that can be paid without appearing, and violations that involve an accident are excluded from that schedule by law. Expect a court date.

Consider talking to an attorney first. This is a misdemeanor, and we don't give legal advice.

## Can the Driver Improvement Program keep the points off?

It can. RSMo 302.302 lists careless and imprudent driving among the violations the program covers, along with the extra 2 points for injury or property damage. The court has to approve it, and you have to finish the 8-hour course within 60 days of your conviction.

CDL holders and out-of-state license holders can't use the program.

## Can speeding in a work zone count as careless and imprudent?

Yes. Driving over a posted work zone speed limit "shall be deemed prima facie evidence of careless and imprudent driving" (RSMo 304.351.7).

## What should I ask the court?

- Is the charge under state law or a city ordinance?
- Will the court approve the Driver Improvement Program for this charge?
- What is my conviction date, so I can count the 60 days?

[How to ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program).

posts.content:
## What does the law say?

RSMo 304.017: a driver "shall not follow another vehicle more closely than is reasonably safe and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicle and the traffic upon and the condition of the roadway."

There's no set distance in the statute. The officer and the court judge what was safe for the speed and conditions.

## What is the fine?

| Vehicle | Fine on the state schedule |
|---|---|
| Car, motorcycle, or truck under 18,000 lbs | $60.50 |
| Truck 18,000 lbs or more, or bus | $130.50 |

Court costs are added. The municipal fine schedule lists the same $60.50 for a car. Look up your case on Case.net to see your total.

## How many points?

Two. Form 899 lists following too close among the violations assessed 2 points under state, county or city law.

## Can I pay it without going to court?

Usually, if there was no crash. Tickets that involve an accident are excluded from the pay-without-appearing schedule.

## Can I keep the 2 points off?

Yes, with the court's approval. Ask for the Driver Improvement Program before you plead guilty or pay. Then finish the 8-hour course within 60 days of your conviction.

## Is it worth using the program for 2 points?

It depends on your record. You can use the program once in 36 months, and points shrink by a third after a year without a new conviction.

If you have 6 points, use it. Two more is a suspension. If your record is clean, you might keep it in reserve. [What 4, 8 and 12 points do](/missouri/blog/missouri-points-what-4-8-12-points-do).

## What is the fine?

| Violation | Fine on the state schedule |
|---|---|
| Failed to stop for a stop sign | $60.50 |
| Failed to stop for a steady red signal | $60.50 |
| Failed to stop for a flashing red signal | $60.50 |

|---|---|---|---|
| Stop sign | 2 | 2 | 1 |
| Red light and other signals | 2 | 2 | 2 |

The 1-point city stop sign applies "where no accident is involved" (RSMo 302.302).

## Where do I have to stop?

At the marked stop line. If there's none, before the crosswalk. If there's no crosswalk, at the point nearest the intersecting road where you can see approaching traffic. Then yield to any vehicle in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

## What if someone was hurt?

The penalties go up. Under RSMo 304.351, a right-of-way violation that caused physical injury carries an added penalty of up to $200, and the court can suspend your license for 30 days. For serious physical injury it's up to $500 and 90 days.

## Can I keep the points off?

Yes, with the court's approval. Both are ordinary moving violations, which the Driver Improvement Program covers. Ask before you plead guilty or pay.

## Should I use the program on a 1-point ticket?

Probably not, unless you're close to 8 points. You get the program once in 36 months. [Check your points](/missouri/blog/check-points-missouri-driving-record) first.

posts.title: Passing a school bus in Missouri: now 5 points
posts.seoTitle: Missouri School Bus Ticket: 5 Points
posts.description: Since August 28, 2026, failing to stop for a school bus in Missouri is 5 points. The fine, the exceptions, and why the course can't keep these off.
posts.answer: Failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children is 5 points in Missouri, under a change that took effect August 28, 2026. The fine on the state schedule is $130.50 plus court costs. The Driver Improvement Program doesn't cover this violation.

faq.q: How many points is passing a school bus in Missouri?
faq.a: Five points, under an amendment to RSMo 302.302 that took effect August 28, 2026.

faq.q: How much is a ticket for passing a school bus in Missouri?
faq.a: The statewide fine schedule lists $130.50, plus court costs.

faq.q: Do I have to stop for a school bus on a four-lane road in Missouri?
faq.a: Not if the bus is going the opposite direction on a highway with four or more lanes, or is on a different roadway.

faq.a: No. The Driver Improvement Program does not cover the school bus violation.

posts.content:
## When do I have to stop?

When you meet or overtake, "from either direction," a school bus that has stopped to receive or discharge school children and whose driver has given the signal to stop (RSMo 304.050). You stay stopped until the bus moves again or the driver signals you to go.

## When don't I have to stop?

- The bus is on a different roadway of a highway with separate roadways.
- The bus is going the opposite direction on a highway with four or more lanes.
- The bus is stopped in a loading zone along a limited-access highway where pedestrians can't cross.

On an ordinary two-lane road, both directions stop.

## What changed in 2026?

The points. RSMo 302.302 now lists failure to stop for a school bus at 5 points, effective August 28, 2026. It appears on the August 2026 revision of the Department of Revenue's Form 899. Charts printed before then don't show it.

## What is the fine?

$130.50 on the statewide fine schedule, plus court costs.

## Can the owner be charged if the driver isn't identified?

Yes. If an officer or the bus driver witnesses the violation and the driver's identity isn't otherwise apparent, the law presumes the registered owner committed it. The owner can rebut that.

## Can the Driver Improvement Program keep the points off?

No. The program covers speeding, careless and imprudent driving and ordinary 2-point moving violations. The school bus violation has its own line in the points table and isn't one of them.

## How close is 5 points to a suspension?

Three points. Missouri suspends at 8 points in 18 months, and one state speeding ticket is 3.

If you get another ticket in the next 18 months, ask the court for the Driver Improvement Program on that one. [How the program works](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-program).

## How do the points come off?

With time. They drop by a third after a year without a new conviction, by half of the rest after two years, and to zero after three.
