posts.description: Missouri's hands-free law bans holding a phone while driving. Fines run up to $150, $250 or $500. It carries no points, and you can't be stopped for it alone.
posts.answer: Missouri's hands-free law bans holding or supporting a phone while driving. The fine is up to $150 for a first conviction, up to $250 for a second within 24 months, and up to $500 for a third or for a violation in a school zone or an active work zone. It carries no points, and an officer can't stop you for this alone.

keyFacts.label: Third, or school or work zone

faq.q: How much is a hands-free ticket in Missouri?
faq.a: Up to $150 for a first conviction, up to $250 for a second within 24 months, and up to $500 for a third or for a violation in a school zone or a work zone with workers present.

faq.q: Does a texting ticket put points on your license in Missouri?
faq.a: No. Department of Revenue Form 899 lists texting while driving as no longer point-assessable after August 28, 2023.

faq.q: Can police pull you over for holding a phone in Missouri?
faq.a: Not for that alone. RSMo 304.822 says no person shall be stopped solely for a violation of the hands-free law.

faq.q: Can I use my phone while stopped in Missouri?
faq.a: The law exempts operators using a device while the vehicle is lawfully stopped or parked.

sources.name: Missouri Revised Statutes 304.822: Siddens Bening Hands Free Law
Missouri Department of Revenue Form 899: violation descriptions and points assessed (revised 08-2026)
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program

posts.content:
## What does the law ban?

The Siddens Bening Hands Free Law, RSMo 304.822, says a driver may not:

- Physically hold or support a phone or other device with any part of the body
- Write, send or read a text, email or social media message
- Make a call, unless it's hands-free
- Type letters, numbers or symbols into a website or app
- Watch a video, other than navigation
- Record, post or broadcast video

## What is allowed?

- Voice-operated and hands-free use
- Using a map for navigation
- Listening to audio
- Using the device while lawfully stopped or parked
- Reporting an emergency

Hands-free means you can start or end a function "with a single touch or single swipe."

## What are the fines?

| Conviction | Fine |
|---|---|
| First in 24 months | Up to $150 |
| Second in 24 months | Up to $250 |
| Third or more in 24 months | Up to $500 |
| In a work zone with workers present, or a marked school zone | Up to $500 |

Citations began January 1, 2025. Before that, officers gave warnings.

## Are there points?

No. The Department of Revenue's Form 899 lists texting while driving as "no longer point assessible" after August 28, 2023.

## Can I be pulled over just for holding my phone?

No. The law says "no person shall be stopped, inspected, or detained solely for a violation of this section." An officer needs another reason for the stop.

## Can the officer search my phone?

You can decline. An officer who stops you for this violation has to tell you that you have the right to decline a search of your device.

## When does it become a crime?

| The violation caused | Offense |
|---|---|
| Property damage over $5,000 | Class D misdemeanor |
| Serious physical injury | Class B misdemeanor |
| Death | Class D felony |

## Do I need a course for this ticket?

No. There are no points to keep off. If you were also cited for speeding or another moving violation at the same stop, that's the ticket to ask the court about. [Which tickets qualify](/missouri/blog/which-tickets-qualify-missouri-driver-improvement).

posts.title: Seat belt tickets in Missouri: $10, no points, no court costs
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Seat Belt Ticket: $10, No Points
posts.description: A Missouri seat belt ticket is a fine of up to $10 with no court costs and no points. Who has to buckle up, and the rule for children under 16.
posts.answer: A seat belt ticket in Missouri is a fine of up to $10. The law bars court costs and points for it, and an adult can't be stopped solely to check for a seat belt. The rules for children under 16 are separate and carry higher fines.

faq.q: How much is a seat belt ticket in Missouri?
faq.a: Up to $10, with no court costs, under RSMo 307.178.

faq.q: Does a seat belt ticket put points on your license in Missouri?
faq.a: No. The statute says in no case shall points be assessed for a seat belt violation.

faq.q: Can you be pulled over for not wearing a seat belt in Missouri?
faq.a: An adult cannot be stopped solely to determine seat belt compliance under RSMo 307.178.

sources.name: Missouri Revised Statutes 307.178: seat belts
Missouri Courts: Statewide Fine Schedule
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program

posts.content:
## Who has to wear a seat belt?

Under RSMo 307.178:

- The driver and front seat passenger of a passenger car
- Anyone under 18 driving or riding in a truck

A passenger car is a vehicle designed to carry ten people or fewer. Trucks licensed at 12,000 pounds or more and motorcycles aren't included.

## What is the penalty?

An infraction with "a fine not to exceed ten dollars." The law goes on: "no court costs shall be imposed," and "in no case shall points be assessed."

## Can I be pulled over for not wearing one?

Not for that alone. The statute says "no person shall be stopped, inspected, or detained solely to determine compliance." It also says noncompliance isn't probable cause for any other violation.

## Who is exempt?

- People with a medical reason
- People in a vehicle being used for agricultural work
- Postal Service employees servicing boxes or making frequent stops

## What about children?

The driver has to secure any child under 16 in the proper restraint under RSMo 307.179. The municipal fine schedule lists these:

| Violation | Fine |
|---|---|
| Child under 8 not in a child restraint or booster | $49.50 |
| Child 80 pounds or more, or over 4 feet 9 inches, not in a booster or belt | $10 |

## Does not wearing a belt affect a crash claim?

It can, a little. It isn't evidence of comparative negligence. With expert evidence that it contributed to the injuries, it can reduce a recovery by no more than 1 percent.

## Do I need a course for this?

No. There are no points. Pay the $10.

posts.title: Driving without insurance in Missouri: points, fines and suspension
posts.seoTitle: Missouri No Insurance Ticket: Points and Fines
posts.description: A Missouri no-insurance conviction can mean 4 points, a suspension, or court supervision with no points. The court picks. What each one means.
posts.answer: Driving without insurance is a misdemeanor in Missouri. On a conviction the court picks one of three outcomes: suspend your license, send the conviction in for 4 points, or order supervision with no points. If you had insurance when the ticket was written, show the court proof and you can't be found guilty.

keyFacts.label: Second or later
keyFacts.value: Fine of $200 to $500, up to 15 days in jail

faq.q: How many points is no insurance in Missouri?
faq.a: Four points, if the court forwards the conviction for points. The court can instead suspend the license or order supervision with no points.

faq.q: What is the fine for driving without insurance in Missouri?
faq.a: A first violation is a class D misdemeanor. A second or later violation carries a fine of $200 to $500 and up to 15 days in jail.

faq.q: What if I had insurance but no proof when I got the ticket?
faq.a: Show the court proof that you were insured when the citation was written. Under RSMo 303.025 you cannot be found guilty in that case.

faq.q: Can I take the Driver Improvement Program for a no insurance ticket?
faq.a: No. The program does not cover it. A court can order supervision in place of points, once in 36 months.

sources.name: Missouri Revised Statutes 303.025: duty to maintain financial responsibility
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.303: court-ordered supervision
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program
Missouri Department of Revenue: License Reinstatement Requirements
13th Judicial Circuit, Boone County: Accounting and Traffic

posts.content:
## What does the law require?

An owner may not operate or register a vehicle, or let someone else drive it, without maintaining financial responsibility (RSMo 303.025). A driver may not drive someone else's vehicle knowing the owner has no insurance, unless the driver's own policy covers it.

## I had insurance but couldn't show the card. What now?

Bring proof to court. The statute says no one shall be found guilty "if the operator demonstrates to the court that he or she met the financial responsibility requirements of this section at the time the peace officer" wrote the citation.

## What are the penalties?

A first violation is a class D misdemeanor. A second or later one carries a fine of $200 to $500 and may bring up to 15 days in jail.

## What does the court do with my license?

One of these, for a Missouri driver:

1. **Suspend your driving privilege** as of the date of the order.
2. **Forward the conviction for 4 points.**
3. **Order supervision in place of points.** With court-ordered supervision, no points are assessed. It can't be used more than once in 36 months.

## Can the Driver Improvement Program keep the points off?

No. The program covers speeding, careless and imprudent driving and ordinary moving violations. A no-insurance conviction has its own line in the points table.

Supervision is the no-points route for this charge, and it's up to the court. Ask the court or the prosecutor about it, or talk to an attorney.

## Can I pay this ticket online?

Often not. The Boone County court, for one, lists "no insurance/no proof of insurance" among the charges that are mandatory appearances and can't be paid online. Check your case on Case.net or call the clerk.

## What does it take to get reinstated?

The requirements depend on the kind of suspension on your record. Call the Department of Revenue at 573-526-2407, or check the letter it sent you.

## How close is 4 points to a suspension?

Halfway. Missouri suspends at 8 points in 18 months. If you get a speeding ticket later, ask for the Driver Improvement Program on that one. [How the program works](/missouri/blog/missouri-driver-improvement-program).

posts.title: Missouri's move over law: what it requires and what it costs
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Move Over Law: Fines and Penalty
posts.description: Missouri drivers must change lanes or slow down for stopped vehicles with flashing lights. A violation is a class A misdemeanor. The fines.
posts.answer: When you approach a stopped vehicle with red, red and blue, amber, or amber and white lights flashing, Missouri law requires you to move to a lane that isn't next to it, or slow down if you can't. A violation is a class A misdemeanor. The state fine schedule lists $80.50 to $150.50 plus court costs.

keyFacts.label: Fine, emergency vehicle with siren and lights
Covers
keyFacts.value: Emergency, tow, utility and road vehicles with lights on

faq.q: What is the move over law in Missouri?
faq.a: Drivers approaching a stationary vehicle with red, red and blue, amber, or amber and white lights must change to a non-adjacent lane when the road allows it, or slow down to a safe speed.

faq.q: How much is a move over ticket in Missouri?
faq.a: The statewide fine schedule lists $80.50 for failing to yield to a stationary vehicle with amber lights and $150.50 for failing to yield to an emergency vehicle with siren and lights, plus court costs.

faq.q: Does the Missouri move over law apply to tow trucks?
faq.a: It applies to any stationary vehicle displaying lighted amber or amber and white lights, as well as red or red and blue lights.

sources.name: Missouri Revised Statutes 304.022: emergency and stationary vehicles
Missouri Courts: Statewide Fine Schedule
Missouri Department of Revenue Form 899: violation descriptions and points assessed (revised 08-2026)
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program

posts.content:
## What does the law require?

RSMo 304.022 covers two situations.

**An emergency vehicle is coming up on you** with its siren on or its red or blue lights showing. Pull as far right as you can, stop, and stay there until it passes.

**A vehicle is stopped with lights flashing.** For a stationary vehicle showing red, red and blue, amber, or amber and white lights:

1. Change to a lane that isn't next to it, if the road has at least four lanes with two going your way and you can do it safely.
2. If you can't change lanes, slow down and keep a safe speed for the conditions.

## Which vehicles does it cover?

Any stationary vehicle showing those lights. That takes in police, fire and ambulance vehicles, and any vehicle stopped with amber or amber and white lights on.

## What is the penalty?

A class A misdemeanor. The statewide fine schedule lists these fines, with court costs added:

| Violation | Fine |
|---|---|
| Failed to yield to a stationary vehicle with amber or amber and white lights | $80.50 |
| Failed to yield to an emergency vehicle sounding a siren and showing red or blue lights | $150.50 |

## How many points?

Form 899 says any moving violation it doesn't list by name is assessed 2 points.

## Can the Driver Improvement Program keep the points off?

Ordinary moving violations are covered, and the court decides. Ask before you plead guilty or pay. [How to ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program).

## What if I hit someone?

Separate and more serious charges apply. RSMo 302.302 lists endangerment of an emergency responder at 4 points and aggravated endangerment at 12. The Driver Improvement Program doesn't cover either.

posts.title: Work zone tickets in Missouri: the extra fines
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Work Zone Ticket: Extra Fines
posts.description: A Missouri work zone ticket adds $35 to the fine. Speeding or passing with workers present adds $250. The extra fines add no points.
posts.answer: A moving violation in a Missouri work zone adds $35 to the regular fine, or $75 for a second offense. Speeding or passing in a work zone with workers present adds $250, or $300 for a second offense, if the warning signs are posted. The extra fines don't add points.

keyFacts.label: Any moving violation in a work zone

faq.q: How much is a speeding ticket in a work zone in Missouri?
faq.a: The regular speeding fine plus $250 for a first offense, or $300 for a second, when workers are present and the warning signs are posted. Otherwise $35 is added.

faq.q: Do work zone tickets add more points in Missouri?
faq.a: No. RSMo 304.582 says the additional fines do not enhance the assessment of points.

faq.q: Do workers have to be present for the $250 work zone fine in Missouri?
faq.a: Yes. A highway worker must be in the zone at the time, and the warning signs must be posted.

sources.name: Missouri Revised Statutes 304.582: fines in work and construction zones
Missouri Courts: Statewide Fine Schedule
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program
Missouri Revised Statutes 304.822: Siddens Bening Hands Free Law

posts.content:
## What are the extra fines?

From RSMo 304.582:

| Violation in a work zone | First | Second or later |
|---|---|---|
| Any moving violation | $35 added | $75 added |
| Speeding or passing, with a highway worker in the zone | $250 added | $300 added |

Each is "in addition to any other fine authorized by law." You don't get both. If the $250 applies, the $35 doesn't.

## When does the $250 apply?

When three things are true:

1. The violation was speeding or passing.
2. A highway worker was in the zone at the time.
3. Signs are posted that say, in substance, "Warning: Minimum $250 fine for speeding or passing in this work zone when workers are present."

Without the signs, the $250 can't be assessed.

## Do work zone tickets have more points?

No. The law says the additional fines "shall not be construed to enhance the assessment of court costs or the assessment of points."

A state speeding ticket in a work zone is 3 points, the same as anywhere else.

## Is passing in a work zone illegal?

Where signs tell drivers to merge and not pass, yes. It's also illegal on a two-lane highway work zone when workers or equipment are working and signs are posted. It's a class C misdemeanor.

## What would a work zone speeding ticket cost?

Take 12 over with workers present and signs posted. The state schedule fine for 11 to 15 over is $80.50. Add $250. That's $330.50 before court costs.

## Can the Driver Improvement Program help?

With the points, yes. Speeding is covered, and a work zone doesn't change that. The court has to approve it. The course doesn't reduce the fine.

## What about phones in a work zone?

A hands-free law violation in a work zone with workers present carries a fine of up to $500. See [Missouri's hands-free law](/missouri/blog/missouri-hands-free-law-ticket).

posts.title: Missouri tickets that carry no points
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Tickets With No Points
posts.description: Speeding by 5 mph or less, seat belt, hands-free and equipment tickets add no points in Missouri. The list, and what each one costs.
posts.answer: Four kinds of Missouri ticket add no points: speeding by 5 mph or less over the limit, seat belt violations, hands-free law violations, and vehicle equipment violations. You still owe the fine, and you still have to respond by the court date.

faq.q: Which tickets have no points in Missouri?
faq.a: Speeding by 5 mph or less over the limit, seat belt violations, hands-free law violations and vehicle equipment violations.

faq.q: Is 5 over a ticket in Missouri?
faq.a: It can be. Speeding by 5 mph or less is an infraction with a fine, but no points are assessed under RSMo 304.009.

faq.q: Do equipment violations add points in Missouri?
faq.a: No. RSMo 302.302 assesses points for moving violations other than a violation of vehicle equipment provisions.

sources.name: Missouri Revised Statutes 304.009: speeding by five miles per hour or less
Missouri Revised Statutes 307.178: seat belts
Missouri Department of Revenue Form 899: violation descriptions and points assessed (revised 08-2026)
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.010: definitions
Missouri Courts: About Responding to Your Ticket
Missouri Courts: Statewide Fine Schedule

posts.content:
## Which tickets have no points?

| Violation | Why there are no points | Fine |
|---|---|---|
| Speeding by 5 mph or less | RSMo 304.009 says no points shall be assessed | $50.50 on the state schedule |
| Seat belt | RSMo 307.178 says in no case shall points be assessed | Up to $10, no court costs |
| Hands-free law | Form 899 lists it as no longer point-assessable | Up to $150 for a first conviction |
| Equipment violations | The points law excludes vehicle equipment provisions | Varies |

## What counts as a moving violation?

Missouri defines it as a traffic violation "where at the time of violation the motor vehicle involved is in motion." The definition leaves out driving without a valid registration and violations of the size and weight laws.

Any moving violation that isn't listed by name on Form 899 is 2 points.

## Do I still have to deal with a no-point ticket?

Yes. The Missouri courts say you must respond by the court date on the citation, by pleading guilty and paying or by appearing. Failing to respond can lead to a suspension and a warrant.

## Should I ask for the Driver Improvement Program on a no-point ticket?

No. The program keeps points off, and there aren't any. You can use it once in 36 months, so save it.

## Can a ticket be changed to one with no points?

That's between you, the prosecutor and the court. We don't give legal advice. An attorney can tell you what's possible in your court.

## Which tickets have the most points?

| Violation | Points |
|---|---|
| Driving while suspended or revoked | 12 |
| Leaving the scene of an accident, state law | 12 |
| Driving while intoxicated, first conviction | 8 |
| Passing a stopped school bus | 5 |
| No insurance | 4 |

[Points by violation](/missouri/blog/missouri-points-by-violation) has the full chart.

posts.title: Missouri hardship license: the Limited Driving Privilege
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Hardship License: Limited Driving Privilege
posts.description: Suspended in Missouri and need to drive to work? You may qualify for a Limited Driving Privilege. Who can't get one, and how to apply on Form 4595.
posts.answer: A Limited Driving Privilege, often called a hardship license, lets a suspended or revoked Missouri driver drive for work and other approved needs. Apply to the Department of Revenue on Form 4595 with an SR-22 insurance filing. The Department reviews applications in about five working days.

faq.q: Can I get a hardship license in Missouri?
faq.a: You may qualify for a Limited Driving Privilege if your license is suspended, revoked or denied and you need to drive for work or other approved needs. Some convictions and suspensions make a driver ineligible.

faq.q: How do I apply for a Limited Driving Privilege in Missouri?
faq.a: Submit Form 4595 to the Department of Revenue with an SR-22 insurance filing, or file a petition with the circuit court in the county where you live or work.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a Limited Driving Privilege in Missouri?
faq.a: The Department of Revenue reviews applications in approximately five working days and mails its decision.

sources.name: Missouri Department of Revenue: Limited Driving Privilege
Missouri Department of Revenue: Tickets and Points FAQ
Missouri Department of Revenue: License Reinstatement Requirements
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.304: suspension, revocation and reinstatement

posts.content:
## What is a Limited Driving Privilege?

The Department of Revenue describes it as a way to drive "in certain pre-approved situations" when your license is suspended, revoked or denied and you aren't yet eligible for reinstatement. It's set out in RSMo 302.309.

## Who can't get one?

The Department's list includes drivers who:

- Are already eligible for reinstatement but haven't met the requirements
- Were convicted in the last five years of a felony involving a motor vehicle
- Have a revocation for failing a driving or medical examination
- Have a suspension for an unpaid accident judgment
- Have a suspension for failure to pay a ticket in Missouri or another state
- Have a suspension from a DWI or excessive blood alcohol conviction, who may qualify for a Restricted Driving Privilege
- Aren't Missouri residents and don't work or attend school in Missouri

It can't be used to drive a commercial motor vehicle.

## How do I apply?

There are two ways.

**Through the Department of Revenue.** Submit Form 4595, Application for Limited Driving Privilege. If there's no SR-22 on file for you, have your insurer send one or include a copy. The Department reviews the application in about five working days and mails you an order granting or denying it.

**Through the circuit court** in the county where you live or work. A filing fee and court costs apply. Drivers with an active 5-year or 10-year denial have to use this route.

## Do I need an ignition interlock?

Only with alcohol offenses. If you have more than one alcohol offense or an active chemical revocation, you submit proof that a device is installed.

## Is it worth applying for a 30-day points suspension?

A first points suspension is 30 days, and review takes about five working days. Call the Department at 573-526-2407 and ask about your record before you decide.

## How do I avoid the suspension?

Keep new points off. If you're at 5 or more and get a ticket, ask the court for the Driver Improvement Program before you plead. [Suspended for points](/missouri/blog/missouri-license-suspended-for-points) explains the thresholds.

posts.title: What is the court originator number for a Missouri driver improvement course?
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Court Originator Number for DIP
posts.description: Online Missouri driver improvement courses ask for your court's originator number. What it is, where to find it, and two examples from court websites.
posts.answer: The court originator number, also called the ORI or state identification number, identifies the court that approved your Driver Improvement Program. It starts with MO and ends with J. Online courses ask for it at sign-up so it appears on your completion form. Get it from your court's website or the clerk.

faq.q: What is a court originator number in Missouri?
faq.a: It is the state's identifying number for a court, in the form MO, six digits and the letter J. Online driver improvement courses ask for it so the completion form names the right court.

faq.q: Where do I find the court ORI number for Missouri driver improvement?
faq.a: On your court paperwork, on the court's website, or from the clerk of the court named on your citation.

faq.q: What is the Boone County court originator number?
faq.a: The Boone County Circuit Court lists its court originator number as MO010033J.

sources.name: 13th Judicial Circuit, Boone County: Accounting and Traffic
Creve Coeur Municipal Court: Driver Improvement Program
Missouri Safety Center: Driver Improvement Program Process
Missouri Revised Statutes 302.302: point system and the driver-improvement program

posts.content:
## What is a court originator number?

It's the state's identifier for a court. Two Missouri courts publish theirs for drivers taking the Driver Improvement Program:

| Court | Number | What the court calls it |
|---|---|---|
| Boone County Circuit Court | MO010033J | Court originator number |
| Creve Coeur Municipal Court | MO095151J | State identification number |

## Why does the course ask for it?

So your completion form names the right court. The Boone County court tells drivers: "In order to participate in an on-line class, you will need the court originator number." Creve Coeur says you "may need" its number "for your application."

## Where do I find mine?

1. Look at your court paperwork.
2. Check the court's website. Search the page for "originator" or "identification number."
3. Call the clerk of the court on your citation and ask for the court's originator number for a Driver Improvement Program.

Don't guess, and don't use another court's number. The completion form goes to the Department of Revenue and has to match your case.

## What else will I need to enroll?

- Your name, date of birth and Missouri driver license number, as they appear on your license
- Your citation or case number
- The court's name
- Your conviction date, which starts the 60 days

## What happens to the completion form?

The course provider gives you MO Form 4444 when you pass. You take it to the court for a signature, and it goes to the Department of Revenue within 15 days. The Boone County court asks for the original certificate to be "forwarded to our office promptly." [Form 4444](/missouri/blog/missouri-form-4444) has the steps.

## Does every court use the same process?

No. Ask your clerk whether the court wants the original, whether it sends the form to the state, and whether it accepts email.

posts.title: How to look up and pay a Missouri ticket on Case.net
posts.seoTitle: Look Up and Pay a Missouri Ticket on Case.net
posts.description: Find a Missouri traffic ticket on Case.net by case number or name, see the fine and costs, and pay with Plead and Pay. The steps, and what to check first.
posts.answer: Search Case.net by case number or by name, open your case, and click Plead and Pay to see the fine and court costs. Looking doesn't plead you guilty. Finishing the payment does. If no Plead and Pay button appears, your ticket needs a court appearance.

faq.q: How do I look up a traffic ticket in Missouri?
faq.a: Search Case.net on the Missouri courts website by case number or by your name and the court.

faq.q: Does clicking Plead and Pay mean I am pleading guilty?
faq.a: No. Clicking the button shows the fine and court costs. You plead guilty only when you complete the process and receive a confirmation.

faq.q: Why is there no Plead and Pay button on my Missouri ticket?
faq.a: The ticket is not eligible to be paid without a court appearance. You must appear in court on the date on the citation.

sources.name: Missouri Courts: Make a Payment (Plead and Pay)
Missouri Courts: About Responding to Your Ticket
Missouri Courts: Plead and Pay FAQs
Kansas City Municipal Court: Ticket Payments and Fines
St. Louis Municipal Court: Pay a Traffic Ticket and Plead Guilty Without a Court Appearance
Missouri Revised Statutes 476.385: schedule of fines and the central violations bureau

posts.content:
## How do I find my ticket?

1. Go to Case.net on the Missouri courts' website.
2. Choose Case Number Search and enter the number from your citation. On a traffic ticket it's in the upper corner.
3. Or choose Litigant Name Search, pick the court, and enter your last name.

City courts use the same system. Kansas City tells drivers to select Jackson County, 16th Judicial Circuit, then Kansas City Municipal. St. Louis tells drivers to select City of St. Louis, 22nd Judicial Court.

Beware of look-alike sites. The Kansas City court passes along a notice from the state courts to avoid fake Case.net websites.

## How do I see what I owe?

Open the case and click Plead and Pay. The button shows the full amount due, fines and court costs together. St. Louis's court says you "can stop here if you do not want to proceed at this time."

## How do I pay?

Select Plead and Pay, click Continue to Plead, and follow the steps. You pay the whole amount, plus a convenience fee for a card. An electronic check has a flat fee of 50 cents.

If you got more than one citation, repeat the process for each.

## What if there's no Plead and Pay button?

The ticket isn't eligible, and you have to appear in court on the date on the citation. See [tickets that require a court appearance](/missouri/blog/missouri-mandatory-court-appearance-tickets).

## What does paying mean?

A guilty plea and a waiver of your hearing. The conviction goes to the Department of Revenue, which assesses the points.

## What should I do before I pay?

Decide about the Driver Improvement Program. It keeps the points off, but the court has to approve it. Call the clerk and ask whether the court will approve it for your ticket and how to request it. [Should you just pay?](/missouri/blog/should-i-pay-my-missouri-ticket-online)

## I already went to court. How do I pay the balance?

Use Pay By Web on Case.net. Payments usually post within one business day. Pay within 30 days of your court date to avoid a time payment fee.

## Will a court call me for payment?

No. The Missouri courts say no one from a court will ever contact you by phone and ask for payment or card information.

posts.title: Missouri tickets that require a court appearance
posts.seoTitle: Missouri Tickets That Require a Court Appearance
posts.description: Some Missouri tickets can't be paid online: accidents, DWI, driving while suspended, and others the court sets. How to tell, and what to do.
posts.answer: State law keeps four kinds of ticket off the pay-without-appearing schedule: violations that caused injury or property damage, driving while intoxicated, driving with a suspended or revoked license, and fleeing an officer. posts.content:
## Which tickets can never be on the fine schedule?

RSMo 476.385 says the schedule can't include offenses involving:

1. "Any violation resulting in personal injury or property damage to another person"
2. Operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated or under the influence
3. Operating a vehicle with a counterfeited, altered, suspended or revoked license
4. Fleeing or attempting to elude an officer

## What do individual courts add?

Each court can require appearances for more. Three examples from court websites:

| Court | Also requires an appearance for |
|---|---|
| Boone County Circuit Court | Driving without a valid license, no insurance or no proof of insurance, speeding in excess of 25 mph, tickets where an accident was involved |
| Columbia Municipal Court | Any violation the prosecutor submits for a court appearance, and any violation for which a summons to appear is issued |
| Kansas City Municipal Court | Any ticket with no fine amount printed on it, and a payable ticket issued along with a non-payable one or during an accident |

## How do I tell which kind I have?

- **Look at the ticket.** Kansas City says a case is non-payable "if no fine amount is printed on your ticket."
- **Look on Case.net.** No Plead and Pay button means the ticket isn't eligible.
- **Call the clerk** of the court on your citation.

If you got several tickets at once, check each one. Some may be payable and others not.

## What happens if I miss the court date?

The courts say your license may be suspended or a warrant may be issued. Kansas City's court says the judge "will issue a failure to appear warrant."

## Can I get a new date?

Ask the court before the date passes. Kansas City allows a first-time continuance if you request it at least three days before the court date on the ticket.

## Is a court appearance bad for keeping points off?

No. It's the place to ask. The Missouri Safety Center says a driver "must appear in court and request the court's permission" for the Driver Improvement Program. If your violation is one the program covers, ask the judge or prosecutor at the appearance.

Speeding more than 25 over is still speeding, which the program covers. DWI, driving while suspended and no insurance aren't covered.

## Should I get an attorney?

For a misdemeanor or anything involving an accident, consider it. We don't give legal advice.

posts.content:
## Where is the Kansas City Municipal Court?

At 511 E. 11th Street, Kansas City, MO 64106. The Violations Bureau is on the first floor. For help, email court@kcmo.org or call 816-513-2700.

## How do I pay a Kansas City traffic ticket?

- **Online.** Search Case.net by case number, or by name with Jackson County, 16th Judicial Circuit, then Kansas City Municipal. Click Payment, then Plead and Pay.
- **By mail.** Check or money order payable to "Municipal Court," to 511 E. 11th Street, Kansas City, MO 64106. No cash.
- **In person.** At the Violations Bureau, the lobby kiosk or the drop box.

Fines on payable tickets are due by the court date on the ticket. The court says minor traffic violations carry up to $225 in total fine and costs.

## Which tickets need a court appearance?

Any ticket with no fine amount printed on it. The court also says a ticket that's normally payable "may be non-payable if it was issued with other non-payable tickets or involves a vehicle accident." If you miss a mandatory date, the judge issues a failure to appear warrant. You can ask for one first-time continuance, at least three days before the court date.

## What does the court say about the Driver Improvement Program?

The Kansas City court pages we read don't describe the Driver Improvement Program. That doesn't mean the court won't approve it. State law gives every court the authority. Call 816-513-2700 or email court@kcmo.org and ask before you pay.

## How do I keep the points off?

Ask the court to let you complete the Driver Improvement Program before you plead guilty or pay. Paying is a guilty plea, and the points follow the conviction. If the court approves it, you have 60 days from your conviction to finish an 8-hour course on the Missouri Safety Center's approved list.

The program covers speeding, careless and imprudent driving and ordinary moving violations. It isn't available to CDL holders or drivers licensed in another state, and you can use it once in 36 months. [How to ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program).

## What if my ticket isn't from Kansas City police?

A ticket from the Highway Patrol or a county deputy goes to the circuit court for the county, not the city court. Kansas City spans more than one county, so use the court named on your citation.

## What happens after the course?

The course provider gives you MO Form 4444. Take it to the court for a signature, then get it to the Department of Revenue within 15 days of finishing. [Form 4444](/missouri/blog/missouri-form-4444).
